https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/ww3-fears.text: Alice Scarsi Updated Sun, September 27, 2026 at 6:59 AM UTC 0 Two F-18 jets were deployed (Image: Getty) Two F-18 jets part of the Spanish air forces and a Romanian military helicopter were dispatched. NATO aircraft were dispatched to the Romanian border overnight after an "aerial target" was detected near the Danube. The Romanian Defence Ministry (MApN) said the country's radar surveillance system spotted the "aerial target" in the Chilia Veche area, close to River Danube, which marks a natural border between the NATO member state and southwestern Ukraine . In a statement shared on X, the ministry added: "The National Military Command Center notified the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations regarding the implementation of population alert measures in the northern part of Tulcea County, and at 23:32, an RO-Alert message was transmitted." Two F-18 jets and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter of the Romanian Air Force, were deployed, the MApN said, to "monitor the situation". The "aerial target" entered the Romanian airspace near the town and followed a route almost parallel to the Chilia arm, the ministry said, citing what radar signals had picked up. The signal with the target was lost in the Pardina area, the ministry added, and the air alert ended at 12.48am local time on September 27. The ministry didn't provide any information on the provenance of the target. This comes after another night of heavy Russian strikes on Ukraine. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said air defence units were once again operating over the Ukrainian capital last night, marking the third consecutive day of attacks on the city. Among other damages recorded, the mayor said a drone fell in the Solomianskyi district, with its blast wave damaging a five-storey residential building. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said a woman was injured overnight in an attack. https://www.newarkadvertiser.co.uk/news/.text: Home News Article Newark crime headlines feature off-road bike court case and drugs offender with powerful hallucinogen By Kris Johnston - kris.johnston@iliffepublishing.co.uk Published: 05:00, 08 October 2026 This week’s crime news included the latest in a court case following a four-year-old’s death and a drug offender caught after having a powerful hallucinogen sent to his home. Meanwhile, who downloaded hundreds of child sexual abuse images avoided jail. Catch up with the latest crime headlines below… Man denies causing four-year-old’s death in tragic crash Four-year-old Robert Henry Steele died after the crash in Newark. Photo: Nottinghamshire Police A man has denied causing the death of a four-year-old in an off-road bike crash in Newark. Robert Henry Steele died after the collision involving an off-road motorbike and a car on Churchill Drive on Sunday, August 30. He had been a passenger on the bike. On Wednesday last week, his father, Robert Steele, 24, of Grange Road in Newark, pleaded guilty to causing his death by dangerous driving. However, 32-year-old Brian Cameron, of Chatsworth Road, has now denied causing death by dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, and causing death by driving while uninsured and unlicensed. He was remanded in custody until his next hearing at Nottingham Crown Court on January 15. Murder victim’s son launches fundraiser to help get her body home to Poland Tributes have been paid to Anna Zukowska, who leaves behind two sons after her death. Photo: Nottinghamshire Police The devastated son of a 52-year-old murder victim is raising funds to bring her back home to Poland. Anna Zukowska was found dead at her home on James Close in Ollerton shortly before 8pm on September 6. Her son Marcin Żukowski has now launched a fundraiser to help cover the costs of bringing his mum back to Poland. Man who imported hallucinogenic drugs from Peru to use in home lab is jailed Scott Kinta has been jailed for five years. Photo: Nottinghamshire Police A drugs offender was caught by police after he arranged to have several packages of a powerful hallucinogen sent to his home. Scott Kinta came to officers' attention in January 2025 when Border Force officers at Coventry Airport intercepted packages posted from Peru. The six packages, each containing about four kilograms of the Class A drug N-Dimethyltryptamine, were addressed to Kinta's former home in Ollerton. Another package, sent by Kinta to an address in Texas, was also intercepted. When a warrant was executed at Kinta's address, officers found what appeared to be a home laboratory in a front bedroom, containing a forensic unit, numerous bottles, jars, petri dishes, syringes, scales and packaging materials. Jenrick turns vigilante to shame shoplifters in social media stunt Newark MP Robert Jenrick confronted alleged shoplifters in his latest social media video. Photo: Screenshot, Robert Jenrick Facebook. Newark’s MP turned vigilante in a new video where he shamed shoplifters. In a new video posted to social media, Robert Jenrick was in the Brixton area of London attempting to catch shoplifters in the act. After spotting several people who have allegedly just taken items from a nearby shop, the MP then followed and confronted them. Police ramp up patrols to crack down on drivers racing along key road Police have been patrolling roads around Middlebeck to crack down on anti-social driving. Photo: Nottinghamshire Police Police have ramped up their patrols amid concerns about drivers racing along Newark’s Southern Link Road. In response to increasing fears raised by residents in the Middlebeck area regarding car cruising and associated anti-social behaviour, the Newark neighbourhood policing team has conducted a targeted operation to address these issues. Over the last two weekends, officers have successfully prevented a recurrence of the reported offences thanks to a combination of high-visibility patrols, proactive policing and engagement with drivers and residents. Two stolen vehicles, a moped and a motorbike, were recovered - both of which were being driven in an anti-social manner. Van theft suspect chased down and arrested on riverbank The stolen van was tracked down in Newark. Photo: Nottinghamshire Police A stolen van was recovered and a suspect arrested within 30 minutes. Police were called shortly after 1pm on Wednesday, September 30 after a Ford Tipper van was stolen from Lombard Street in Newark. By 1.17pm, the vehicle had been tracked down in the Tolney Lane area. Then, by 1.30pm, a suspect had been chased down and detained on the banks of the River Trent. The 32-year-old was arrested on suspicion of theft and driving while disqualified. He was later released on police bail. 20-year-old driver who left man with serious injuries avoids jail Nottingham Crown Court A driver who left a man with serious injuries after a collision has avoided jail. Tommy Norton, 20, admitted causing serious injury by careless driving following the incident on The Hollows in Maplebeck on May 2, 2025. He had been driving a a Toyota C-HR at the time. Norton, of Hossack Road in Ipswich, Suffolk, pleaded guilty on August 28 this year, with the case subsequently adjourned for a pre-sentence report to be carried out. At Nottingham Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday, he was handed an 18-week jail sentence, suspended for 12 months. Man who downloaded hundreds of child sex abuse images avoids jail A 62-year-old man who downloaded hundreds of child sexual abuse images has avoided jail. Keith Bateman, of Henson Close in Radcliffe, appeared at Nottingham Crown Court yesterday after admitting making 82 category A indecent images - the most serious. He also downloaded 570 category C photos, as well as one uncategorised image and four further prohibited photos. Bateman was spared jail and instead handed a two-year community order. He will be the subject of sexual harm prevention order for five years, and will be placed on the sex offenders register for ten years. His mobile phone will be forfeited, while he will pay a £114 victim surcharge. Crime Newark Kris Johnston MOST READ
